# issuance-client-properties

<!-- Generated by tools/config-reference.py from servlets/attestation-issuer/src/main/resources/META-INF/oidf-settings/issuance-client-properties.json. Do not edit: change the catalogue, then run python3 tools/config-reference.py. -->

The settings of the `issuance-client-properties` component of `servlets/attestation-issuer`, read by package `com.pingidentity.ps.oidf.servlet.attestation`: generated from its catalogue, issuance-client-properties.json, by `tools/config-reference.py`, and checked in CI. [How to read a row](README.md#reading-a-row).

Under the production profile a violation by one of these settings refuses `ATTESTATION_ISSUER` (components).

| Setting | Default | What it does | When it's wrong | Profile | Security |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `attestation_issuer` (extended property) | Unset | The iss of the attestations minted for this client; a client without it is not an attestation client | **Per request**: Missing: the client is unknown to the attester. PingFederate drops an extended property it has not been told about (F-0041), so each is declared server-side | Any | Yes |
| `attestation_issued_ttl` (extended property) | `300`; seconds, 1 to 64800 | How long a minted attestation lives, in seconds, and never past the evidence; at most OIDF_ATTESTER_MAX_ISSUED_TTL, and never above 64800 (the AI Agent Profile's 18-hour ceiling) | **Per request**: Not a whole number of seconds from 1 to 64800, or above OIDF_ATTESTER_MAX_ISSUED_TTL in production: the client's configuration is refused (invalid_client, naming the property, never its value) and the attester skips the client with a warning. Above the cap in development: clamped to the cap with a warning | Any | Yes |
| `attestation_spiffe_bundle` (extended property) | Unset; a JSON object | The trust bundle, an inline JWK Set, that verifies this client's evidence; this or attestation_bundle_url is required for every evidence type but a wallet instance attestation | **Per request**: Not a JSON object, not a JWK Set, or one with no keys: the client's configuration is refused (invalid_client, naming the property) and the attester skips the client with a warning | Any | Yes |
| `attestation_bundle_url` (extended property) | Unset; an http or https URL | Where the trust bundle is fetched from (and cached) at issuance, in place of attestation_spiffe_bundle; the fetch is held to the outbound fetch rules, with no operator exemption | **Per request**: Not an http or https URL: the client's configuration is refused (invalid_client, naming the property) and the attester skips the client with a warning - from 0.6.0; before, it failed at the fetch. Unreachable with nothing cached, or unreachable for 600 s (twice the 300 s cache TTL) since the last successful fetch: that client's issuance fails (server_error) until a fetch succeeds - from 0.8.0; before, the last copy fetched was served for as long as the fetch kept failing | Any | Yes |
| `attestation_entitlement` (extended property) | Unset | The client's RFC 9396 authorization_details ceiling, a JSON array held to the RAR models when the configuration is parsed; an instance's own ceiling must sit within it | **Per request**: Not a JSON array, or one the models refuse: the client's configuration is refused (invalid_client) and the attester skips the client with a warning | Any | Yes |
| `attestation_signing_key_ref` (extended property) | Unset | The OpenBao transit key this client's attestations are signed with; exactly one of this and attestation_signing_jwk. Must be listed in OIDF_ATTESTER_SIGNING_KEYS for the client's attestation_issuer (required in production; X-B04, F-0625) | **Per request**: Both or neither set: invalid_client at issuance. Not listed in OIDF_ATTESTER_SIGNING_KEYS for the client's issuer, or the list unset in production: invalid_client at issuance and attestation.issuer.signing_key_refused. Set with no OpenBao configured: server_error | Any | Yes |
| `attestation_signing_jwk` (extended property) | Unset; a secret, never shown | The private key this client's attestations are signed with, as an inline JWK; exactly one of this and attestation_signing_key_ref. Development only (X-B04, F-0626): production signs with OpenBao transit keys, so the private key never enters PingFederate | **Per request**: Set in production: only this client is refused (invalid_client, attestation.issuer.client_refused naming the property) and the attester skips it while the others issue; move the key to OpenBao and set attestation_signing_key_ref. Not a JSON object: the client's configuration is refused (invalid_client) and the attester skips the client with a warning. Not a usable key: invalid_client at issuance | Not in production: any value | Yes |
| `attestation_instances` (extended property) | Unset | The client's instance bindings, a JSON array of objects: each a subject (spiffe_id, or a wallet instance's id), an optional entitlement ceiling within the client's, and metadata, and optional conditional_ceilings rules of its own (see attestation_conditional_ceilings) | **Per request**: Not a JSON array of objects, or a ceiling the models refuse: the client's configuration is refused (invalid_client) and the attester skips the client with a warning | Any | Yes |
| `attestation_conditional_ceilings` (extended property) | Unset | The client's conditional ceilings (plan item X-B09), a JSON array of up to 16 rules, each {"require": {"<source>:<name>": [values]}, "ceiling": [authorization_details]}: at issuance a rule the instance's verified selectors do not satisfy (for each selector named, at least one of its values) has its ceiling intersected into the instance's, so missing evidence never widens a grant. Applied with each instance's own conditional_ceilings in attestation_instances; nothing left is access_denied | **Per request**: Not a JSON array of rules, a rule with an unknown member, an empty require, a name that is not <source>:<name>, a value that is not a string, or a ceiling the models refuse: the client's configuration is refused (invalid_client) and the attester skips the client with a warning | Any | Yes |
| `attestation_trust_domain` (extended property) | Unset | The trust domain the client's evidence must belong to: pinned for SPIFFE evidence when set; required for the cloud evidence types, whose SPIFFE path it anchors; and, for wallet-instance-attestation, the wallet provider pin, required from 0.8.0: the entity id of the one wallet provider whose WIAs the client accepts | **Per request**: Missing for a cloud evidence type or for wallet-instance-attestation: the client's configuration is refused (invalid_client, and the client_refused event with property=attestation_trust_domain, reason missing) and the attester skips the client with a warning. A wallet provider other than the one named: each of its WIAs is refused, counted under check=pin | Any | Yes |
| `attestation_evidence` (extended property) | `spiffe-jwt`; one of `spiffe-jwt`, `gke-sa-token`, `gcp-id-token`, `eks-sa-token`, `aws-sts-web-identity`, `aks-sa-token`, `azure-mi-token`, `wallet-instance-attestation` | The evidence type the client's instances present | **Per request**: Not one of the types, in any case (before 0.6.0 only the lower-case spelling was taken): the client's configuration is refused (invalid_client) and the attester skips the client with a warning | Any | Yes |
| `attestation_evidence_issuer` (extended property) | Unset | The iss the client's cloud evidence must carry (a cluster's or an account's issuer), which may only narrow the deployment's pins: it must be one of the issuers OIDF_ATTESTER_<TYPE>_ISSUERS pins for the client's evidence type (from 0.6.0, the tighten-only rule of plan item S-4c applied to the attester); unset, any issuer the type's setting pins | **Per request**: Not one of the issuers the type's setting pins, or set for a type with no pin under the production profile: the client's evidence is refused (invalid_client, naming the setting and never the value). Under development, with the type unpinned, it is the client's pin. Evidence from another issuer is refused at issuance (invalid_instance_attestation, 400) | Any | Yes |
| `attestation_asserted_context_resolver` (extended property) | Unset | The asserted-context resolver (entra-directory) this client opts into: every request must then carry asserted_context of the resolver's type (entra-agent-id), resolved only for evidence the directory entry is bound to, and its ceiling only narrows the evidenced one (from 0.8.0 read off a PingFederate client, F-0230; required once set, F-0655). Not read from a CIMD or federation client | **Per request**: Names a resolver this attester has not registered (entra-directory needs OIDF_ENTRA_AGENT_DIRECTORY): the client is refused at load (attestation.issuer.client_refused, property attestation_asserted_context_resolver, reason refused) and its requests invalid_client. Set on a client whose callers send no asserted_context: each request is refused 400 invalid_request. Before 0.8.0 it was ignored on a PingFederate client and the evidenced ceiling applied unnarrowed | Any | Yes |
| `attestation_asserted_context_policy` (extended property) | Unset | Reserved for the asserted-context policy that plan item X-B10's Microsoft Graph resolver (package B10B) defines; it has no meaning yet | **Per request**: Set to anything: the client's configuration is refused (invalid_client, reason refused) and the attester skips the client with a warning, so a setting that does nothing is never mistaken for one that narrows | Any | Yes |
